children: A fairly common and minor smartphone accessory has now been brought into the compulsory product-quality regime, in a move that can formalise the market and open up a Made-in-India ecosystem.  A MeitY (Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology) notification released on Monday now brings smartphone screen protectors  under the mandatory quality certification in India.
From April 2027, the products covered by the notification titled “Glass Screen Protectors,” will  have to comply with the Indian Standard IS 19348:2025.

The introduction of mandatory BIS standards for this product is  viewed by the electronics industry as a welcome step towards building a quality-led, Made-in-India ecosystem   as well as opening up export opportunities. Hiterto, the glass layer protecting smartphones was largely a part of the unorganised market and importers and manufacturers now have to ensure that products comply with specified quality standards.

Ashok Gupta, Executive Chairman, Optiemus Infracom Ltd, said the move can unlock significant opportunities for local value addition, employment generation and the growth of MSMEs and allied industries across the value chain. “At Optiemus Infracom, we are building on our existing screen-protector manufacturing capabilities, with a planned additional capacity of 2 crore units, to meet emerging demand and contribute to the growth of the domestic ecosystem,” he said.

Last year, Optiemus in partnership with Corning launched a premium ‘tempered glass screen protectors’ brand ‘RhinoTech.’ According to the partnership, Corning will supply glass for the screen protectors, while Optiemus will perform the chemical processing at its Noida plant.
“We see this not merely as an opportunity to serve the Indian market, but to build globally competitive capabilities and an export-oriented manufacturing ecosystem,” Gupta added.

Pankaj Mohindroo, Chairman, ICEA (India Cellular & Electronics Association), said that bringing smartphone screen protectors under the CRO is a significant step towards making quality a core pillar of India’s electronics ecosystem.
“Mandatory BIS certification from 1 April 2027 will protect consumers from sub-standard products while creating a level playing field for domestic manufacturers and global companies alike,” he said.

ICEA pegs the market at over 500 million units a year and said the move will catalyse a ₹12,000–16,000 crore quality-driven industry, generate around 60,000 direct and indirect jobs and contribute an estimated ₹2,000 crore in GST revenue.

Faisal Kawoosa, founder, Techarc,  said that the screen protector market is quite lucrative, especially for the non-premium smartphone market, and the BIS standard is a good step to help localise such adjacent industries. “These interventions will help weed out the unbranded / lesser known sellers helping recognised brands to gain. This gets them predictability in demand and helps them plan for manufacturing,” he added.

title: Smartphone screen protectors to comply with quality standards from April 2027, paving way for formalisation
